body_text:
Let $T : V \to V$ be a linear operator on a finite-dimensional
space $V$. If $A = [T]_{\mathcal{B}}$ and
$A' = [T]_{\mathcal{B}'}$ represent $T$ with respect to two
ordered bases $\mathcal{B}$ and $\mathcal{B}'$, then:
$$ A' = P^{-1} A P, $$ where
$P = [I]_{\mathcal{B}'}^{\mathcal{B}}$ is the invertible
change-of-basis matrix.

Two matrices $A, A'$ related by $A' = P^{-1}AP$ are called
*similar*. All similarity invariants—including the determinant
$\det(T)$, trace $\operatorname{tr}(T)$, characteristic polynomial
$\chi_T(t)$, minimal polynomial $m_T(t)$, and eigenvalues with
algebraic and geometric multiplicities—are intrinsic properties of
the linear transformation $T$, completely independent of
coordinate choices.
